headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: OpenHands can read/write mounted files and use broad egress, while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can send API calls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not explicit, but OpenHands can read mounted files and use MCP, while dbt-core can interact with warehouse data and APIs. If dbt artifacts or generated files are placed in the shared runtime, OpenHands could ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default agent workflows, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF dbt-generated files are mounted into OpenHands' runtime
IF OpenHands reads those files as task context or instructions
IF an MCP server forwards dbt output without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dbt artifacts into agent prompts
Separate dbt outputs from OpenHands runtime mounts
Add a provenance header check before any file is treated as instructions
Restrict MCP servers to read-only, allowlisted endpoints
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/ მონაცემ separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and OpenHands can read files in its runtime and has broad network egress. If warehouse extracts, logs, or model artifacts are mounted into OpenHands, they can be exfiltrated to a third-party model provider or other APIs. The pair therefore creates a default-dangerous leakage path with potentially sensitive data exposure.
conditions: IF warehouse data or derived artifacts are mounted into OpenHands
IF OpenHands sends runtime context to a model provider or external API
IF the mounted files include sensitive warehouse rows, credentials, or logs
mitigations: Remove sensitive warehouse exports from the shared runtime
Use a redaction step before any file is opened by OpenHands
Limit OpenHands network egress to approved endpoints only
Rotate any secrets that may already be present in mounted files
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses, while dbt-core can call warehouse APIs and is commonly used to generate project files. If both operate on the same workspace, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or git state without locking. That overlap is dangerous by default because the profiles show no coordination primitive.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted workspace
IF dbt-core writes generated files while OpenHands edits the same paths
IF git state is shared without an external lock
mitigations: Use separate worktrees for dbt-core and OpenHands
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo
Add a manual lock file for shared paths
Review git diffs before any commit or push
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and shell commands, so if it consumes dbt outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or commits. dbt-core produces warehouse-facing artifacts, but the profiles do not show verification between them. The pathway exists in default agent workflows, though the blast radius is usually bounded to work products rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF OpenHands treats dbt output as ground truth without validation
IF dbt-generated facts are used to drive shell edits or commits
IF no human review occurs before downstream actions
mitigations: Require a validation step before OpenHands acts on dbt output
Compare dbt artifacts against source SQL or schema metadata
Block auto-commit until a human approves the diff
Add a checklist for assumptions extracted from dbt output
requires-engineering: wire structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while OpenHands handles files in a Docker runtime and may send context to a configured model provider. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA terms, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I choose medium because the data-class overlap exists and uncertainty should escalate rather than down-rank.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated or region-bound records
IF OpenHands forwards those records to a non-compliant model provider
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Confirm the data residency of the model provider
Exclude regulated rows from any OpenHands prompt or file mount
Document retention settings for both tools
Review whether a DPA is required before use
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
